# Creating a Set in Python
set_one = {"THIS", "IS", "A", "SET"}

print(set_one)

# Removing the data from a set
set_one.clear() # clears the data from set
print(set_one)

# Creating a Set in Python
set_one = {"ONE", "TWO", "THREE"}
set_two = {"THREE", "FOUR", "FIVE"}

# union returns the data present
# in two sets (with no duplicates)
print(set_one.union(set_two))

# intersection returns the data
# present in both the sets
print(set_two.intersection(set_one))

# intersection_update method clears
# the set and updates the set
# with the data common to both sets
set_one.intersection_update(set_two)
print(set_one)

# Creating a Set in Python
set_one = {"ONE", "TWO", "THREE", "FOUR", "FIVE"}
set_two = {"THREE", "FOUR", "FIVE"}

# issubset method checks is the set passed in
# the argument is a subset of calling set.
print(set_one.issubset(set_two)) # Returns False

# issuperset method checks is the set passed in
# the argument is a superset of calling set.
print(set_one.issuperset(set_two)) # Returns True

set_one = {"ONE", "TWO"}
set_two = {"THREE", "FOUR"}

# isdisjoint method checks if the two sets
# doesn't have any common elements
print(set_two.isdisjoint(set_one)) # Returns True

# Creating a Set in Python
set_one = {"ONE", "TWO", "THREE"}
set_two = {"THREE", "FOUR", "FIVE"}

# Data present in set_one and not present in set_two
# Both set_one and set_two won't be updated
# Returns {'ONE', 'TWO' 'FOUR', 'FIVE'} not necessarily in same order
print(set_one.symmetric_difference(set_two))

# Data present in set_one and not present in set_two
# set_one would be updated with difference between two sets
# set_one is updated with {'ONE', 'TWO', 'FOUR', 'FIVE'}
set_one.symmetric_difference_update(set_two)
